title: A workout in progress can be lost without a word if the phone cannot read it back at start-up
what: When the app reopens, it reads back the workout that was in progress. If that read fails, the app quietly treats it as no workout at all and writes nothing to the log. The next workout the member starts then saves over the one that was in progress.
expected: A failed read back is logged and the saved workout is kept (or tried again) so it is never overwritten by a new start.
fix_line: Log the failed read, keep the saved workout and retry it before allowing a new start to replace it

title: Changing how an exercise's weight is counted can fail to be kept without a word
what: Switching an exercise between 'kg each' and 'as one' changes the card at once, but the save for future workouts throws its error away. If it fails, the next workout goes back to the old counting and the member is never told.
expected: A failed save is logged and the member is told the change only applies to this workout.
fix_line: Log the failure and show a short note when the counting could not be kept

title: Renaming a routine can quietly stop its imported workouts counting as its own
what: When a routine is renamed, the app moves its imported workouts (known only by the old name) over to it. If that step fails, the error is thrown away, so those workouts drop out of the routine's history and Previous values with no log.
expected: The failure is logged and the rename either retries the move or tells the member.
fix_line: Log the failure and retry the move with the rename

title: Two different rules decide whether two workout names are the same
what: The phone matches a workout to its routine by name in two places with two rules. One folds every capital letter and every kind of space; the other, inside the database, folds only A to Z and only tabs and line breaks. A name that differs only in a non-English capital letter or an unusual space matches in one place and not the other, so Previous values and history can miss a workout.
expected: One name rule, used in both places.
fix_line: Store a ready-folded name key once and compare that everywhere

title: The name of the saved in-progress workout is typed out separately in three places
what: The storage name of the workout in progress is written out by hand in the workout code, in the exercise-merge code and in the delete-my-data list. If one is changed, merging an exercise would stop updating the open workout, or delete-my-data would leave it behind, with nothing failing. Small list-reading helpers are also copied three times.
expected: One shared name and one shared helper.
fix_line: Move the name and the helper into one shared place

title: An old Undo for body entries is unused by the app but is the one the delete-Undo test checks
what: The Body screen undoes changes with a newer Undo. The older single-entry Undo for a weight or a measurement is no longer used by any screen, yet one test still checks a deleted entry comes back through that old path, so it proves nothing about what members use.
expected: The old Undo is removed and the delete test uses the Undo the screen calls.
fix_line: Delete the old Undo and point its test at the one the screen uses

title: No test checks exercise lists refresh after a new exercise is made, or the Progress lift pick
what: The small switch that makes every exercise list read again after an exercise is created, renamed, merged or hidden, and the pick handed back to Progress, are imported by no test. A break would only show on a phone.
how_often: only after a change breaks it
fix_line: Add a short test that makes an exercise and checks the list re-reads

title: Workout tests wait a fixed few milliseconds of real time for a save to land
what: Tests of the live workout wait a real 10 to 30 milliseconds and then expect the save to have happened, or to have reached a certain point. On a slow cloud runner that may not be long enough, so the test can fail now and then, or pass without testing the race it names.
expected: Tests wait on the save itself (or use a fake clock), never on a fixed real wait.
fix_line: Wait on the write queue going idle instead of a fixed delay
